title: Scaling Reads, Writes & Sharding
summary: Pick storage engines, partition keys, caches, and hot-key defenses that hold up under skew.
body:
Most scaling bottlenecks reduce to either read amplification, write contention on a single node, or skewed hot keys.

## Scaling reads
- Indexing and read replicas: start with composite indexes matching `(equality_predicates, sort_column)` and asynchronous read replicas when slight staleness is acceptable.
- Cache-aside (look-aside): application checks an in-memory cache, loads from DB on miss, and populates with a jittered TTL.
- Stampede protection: use single-flight request coalescing or short leases so `10,000` concurrent misses on an expired key trigger one DB read, not `10,000`.
- Hot-key mitigation: replicate hot read keys across `K` suffixed cache slots (`key#1..key#K`) or add a tiny `1-5s` in-process L1 cache on app servers.

## Scaling writes and storage engines
- B-tree relational stores excel at strong ACID transactions, secondary indexes, and low-latency point reads.
- LSM-tree stores (`WAL + memtable + immutable SSTables + background compaction`) turn random writes into sequential disk I/O for massive write ingestion (logs, chat history, time series, key-value stores).
- Partitioning: shard by a key that co-locates each query's working set (`conversation_id`, `tenant_id`, `event_id`) using consistent hashing with virtual nodes.

## Handling write skew and multi-tenancy
- Hot counters and streams: pre-aggregate in memory over micro-batches on ingestors or salt keys (`item_id#0..15`) and sum across shards on read.
- Multi-tenant whale isolation: pack small tenants onto shared `tenant_id`-prefixed shards while isolating giant enterprise tenants onto dedicated pods and search indices.
